title: Foreign Exchange, Money Markets and Derivatives
overview: The global foreign exchange (FX) and money markets represent the largest and most dynamic financial markets worldwide, with daily FX transactions exceeding $5 trillion. These markets play a critical role in funding, trading, and investment activities, serving as the bridge between various components of global capital markets.

This course provides participants with a comprehensive understanding of the instruments and activities within the international FX and money markets. It emphasizes the integrated nature of FX, money markets, and derivatives, offering participants insights into their mechanics, risks, and opportunities. The course also draws on lessons from the 2007-09 financial crisis and the latest developments, equipping attendees with knowledge on liquidity management, arbitrage, hedging, and risk management
audience: The course is designed for professionals in banking, asset management, and corporate finance, including wealth managers, auditors, accountants, finance specialists, risk managers, and treasury professionals.
methodology: The program employs diverse learning techniques, including interactive presentations, case studies, hands-on Excel model analysis, and workshops, ensuring practical application of concepts.
competencies: Mastery of exchange rate and interest rate risk management
Understanding global FX and money market dynamics
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Understand the FX market's structure, key players, and mechanics.
Analyze the impact of central banks on FX and money markets.
Explore money supply mechanisms, open market operations, and quantitative easing.
Evaluate liquidity, capital adequacy, and solvency issues.
Gain proficiency in global money market instruments and derivatives, including forwards, swaps, and options.
Develop strategies for financial risk management using FX, money market instruments, and derivatives.
